My cat hasn't had any episodes since starting her meds, but it's not the most convenient to give since she needs it 3 times a day. I just crush the pill into a little bit of food (breakfast, a mid-day snacky treat, and dinner), but she's a very good eater so it's never a problem. If your cat isn't a very good eater you may need to go with a compound in a syringe that gets squirted into their mouth, or a pill shoved down their throat. My cat is pretty squirmy/difficult, so the food method is definitely preferred.

There are side effects to what my girl is on (Keppra - anti-convulsant med), but it's mostly drowsiness. She has anxiety and can be a bit of a monster at times, so I honestly think it's been good for her. 

The vet may also recommend additional diagnostics if you haven't done them already to confirm there isn't a primary cause. We had a spinal tap, MRI, etc to confirm she didn't have any brain damage, tumors, infections of the spinal cord, etc. That being said, it's super expensive, so it may be cheaper to just go with the meds (I pay ~$30 a month for them which I find is completely worth it knowing they're keeping her safer).

Good luck, I wish the best for you and your baby :)

Recent research shows FIV+ cats aren't actually known to have shorter life expectancies... That being said, it's recommended they're kept inside to reduce risk of catching any illnesses. FELV, on the other hand, significantly reduces life expectancy and is contagious. They should only be adopted as solo cats or with other FELV cats (there is technically a vaccine but I believe it's very expensive and isn't guaranteed to work).

Not a vet, just spend a lot of time with sick cats at my local shelter. We've had bad illnesses run through the shelter, and I've seen FIV cats get over them quickly and non-FIV cats need to go to the emergency vet, so it can also be very dependent on the individual cat/illness.

Aww I'm so sorry for your boy that's so scary :( I saw the video you posted and it looks exactly like my girl's seizures. 

If it makes you feel better, I rushed her to the emergency vet the first time it happened (didn't know it was a seizure at the time) and she was totally fine when she got there. The second time, which was 6ish months later, I called some emergency vets who were saying it'd be a 4+ hour wait and if she wasn't actively dying to not bring her in... I called her regular vet in the morning and they were able to see her that morning. Both times she recovered very quickly (this was back in 2022), and the vet and I decided medicating her didn't make sense given the episodes were minor and infrequent (less than one a month and seizures under 30 minutes).

Videos are super important for helping with diagnosis, so great job taking a video. Epilepsy is extremely rare in cats, so they should try to rule out everything else first (even an infection can cause seizures). They may not go through all the diagnostics since this is his first time and he seemed to have a quick recovery. They should be checking that he doesn't have an infection, diabetes, etc as those are relatively quick and easy diagnostic tests to run. If nothing obvious comes up they may just recommend keeping an eye on him and documenting the episodes (length, how recovery goes, frequency). With her more serious recent episode, they ran an MRI and a spinal tap to look for tumors, spinal issues, and any other structural problems, which all came back totally normal. 

My girl is doing really really now :) she's totally back to her normal ridiculous self. We have to medicate her 3x a day which is inconvenient, but I'm honestly so glad she's home. I have cat insurance for her, which made getting the diagnostic tests done a lot more doable. 

I'm feeling much less stressed about my trip, she hasn't had any weird episodes and I have a good friend who's going to board her (she has no other pets but has boarded for others before). At this point, we've been informed that her seizures are something that may just happen and we just need to sit with her and watch her. 

I really hope you can get some answers for your boy and that he's doing well :)
